title: Indian-Origin Psychiatrist Swaran Singh Named to UK House of Lords in New Peerages Announcement
excerpt: The University of Warwick professor and former Equality and Human Rights Commissioner will join Britain's upper chamber as part of the July 2026 political peerages.
body:
Professor Swaran Singh, an Indian-origin psychiatrist at the University of Warwick, has been named among new life peers set to join the UK's House of Lords as part of the July 2026 political peerages — a significant recognition of his contributions to British public life and mental health policy.

## Who Is Swaran Singh?

Singh is a Professor of Social and Community Psychiatry at the University of Warwick, a position he has held since 2006. He also serves as a consultant psychiatrist at the Coventry and Warwickshire Partnership NHS Trust, working directly with patients while conducting research into mental health inequalities and community-based psychiatric care.

Beyond his academic and clinical work, Singh has held prominent public service roles. He served as a commissioner on the Equality and Human Rights Commission, the UK's national equality body responsible for enforcing the Equality Act and promoting human rights protections across England, Scotland, and Wales.

## The July 2026 Peerages

Singh's peerage was announced as part of a batch of new appointments formally gazetted on July 16, 2026, by GOV.UK. He will sit as a Conservative peer — joining two other Conservative nominees, entrepreneur David Ross (co-founder of Carphone Warehouse) and General Sir Patrick Sanders (former Chief of the General Staff).

The July 2026 peerages also include Labour nominations such as former London Mayor Sadiq Khan and broadcaster June Sarpong, as well as Crossbench nominees including Sir Brian Leveson, who led the landmark Leveson Inquiry into press ethics.

## A Milestone for the Indian Diaspora in Britain

Singh's appointment adds to a growing list of Indian-origin individuals serving at the highest levels of British governance. The House of Lords, which scrutinizes legislation, investigates government activity through committee work, and holds the government to account through questions and debates, currently comprises 772 members.

His expertise in mental health inequalities and community psychiatry is expected to bring a valuable perspective to Lords debates on healthcare policy, equality, and public health — areas of increasing importance in post-pandemic Britain.

The announcement comes amid broader debates about reform of the House of Lords. The House of Lords (Hereditary Peers) Act 2026, which received Royal Assent in March, ended the right of hereditary peers to sit and vote, meaning the upper chamber now comprises only life peers and the Lords Spiritual.

*Sources: GOV.UK Political Peerages July 2026, UK Parliament records*
author: Diaspora Desk
